title: Sterling Airways 296
summary: Sterling Airways Flight 296, a Caravelle, crashed into a mountain ridge on approach to Dubai on March 14, 1972. The investigation found that the crew descended below the minimum prescribed altitude due to incorrect information from an outdated flight plan and misreading of the weather radar, which led them to believe they were closer to Dubai than they actually were.
probable_cause: The pilots descended below minimum prescribed altitude during approach. This was attributed to incorrect information on the outdated flight plan and/or misreading of the weather radar which gave the pilots false impression of their proximity to the destination airport.

factors.evidence: incorrect information on the outdated flight plan and/or misreading of the weather radar led the pilots to believe they were closer to Dubai than they actually were
Beginning at 21:47 the controllers experienced communication problems with Flight 296
the pilots descended below the minimum prescribed altitude
crashed into a mountain ridge on approach to Dubai in Al Hayl, Fujariah

events.text: Crew reported passing SALMON waypoint, climbing from FL250 to FL310
Beginning at 21:47 the controllers experienced communication problems with Flight 296 but managed to re-establish communication at 22:04
Crew passed BLUE WHALE waypoint 3 to 6 minutes earlier than expected, suggesting navigation error
Crew reported DOLPHIN waypoint and contacted Dubai Tower at 22:15
Crew descended below minimum prescribed altitude believing they were closer than actual
Aircraft struck mountain ridge on approach to Dubai

notes: Outdated flight plan contributed to navigation error
Communication problems with ATC during flight

title: British European Airways 548
summary: Hawker Siddeley Trident entered a deep stall during initial climb shortly after takeoff from Heathrow and descended steeply until crashing near Staines. The aircraft had not achieved sufficient airspeed and high-lift devices were not properly configured for the climb phase. The public inquiry principally blamed the captain for failing to maintain airspeed and configure the aircraft correctly. The captain had an undiagnosed heart condition and the co-pilot had limited experience. The aircraft's T-tail design and high-lift system made it vulnerable to deep stall if airspeed was insufficient and high-lift devices were not extended.
probable_cause: The captain failed to maintain sufficient airspeed and failed to extend high-lift devices properly during initial climb, causing the aircraft to enter a deep stall from which recovery was impossible. The captain's undiagnosed heart condition may have contributed to impaired judgment. An unspecified technical problem apparently resolved before takeoff and limited co-pilot experience with the aircraft also contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: Captain failed to maintain airspeed and configure high-lift devices correctly for climbing phase.
Captain had an undiagnosed heart condition.
Co-pilot had limited experience and was not qualified as pilot-flying for the aircraft.
Trident aircraft with T-tail arrangement had potentially dangerous deep stall characteristics if airspeed insufficient and high-lift devices not extended.
Aircraft entered a deep stall in the third minute of its flight.
Aircraft descended steeply after deep stall with no recovery possible.
Aircraft crashed into ground near Staines-upon-Thames narrowly missing busy main road.

events.text: Aircraft takes off from runway at Heathrow despite industrial disruption loading aircraft to maximum allowed weight.
Aircraft begins initial climb but captain fails to maintain sufficient airspeed and fails to configure high-lift devices properly.
Aircraft enters deep stall in third minute of flight, stall warning stick shaker activates but crew unable to recover.
Aircraft descends steeply from deep stall, control surfaces become ineffective in stalled wing turbulence zone.
Aircraft crashes into ground near Staines, narrowly missing busy main road, all 118 people on board killed.

title: Interflug 450
summary: Interflug Flight 450 with 156 aboard took off from Berlin-Schönefeld at 16:30. At 16:43, thirteen minutes into flight at 8900 m altitude, the crew reported problems with elevators and was approximately 10 degrees off course. At 16:51 the crew began fuel dump. Flight attendants reported smoke in the rear section of the cabin. At 16:59:25 the crew issued a mayday indicating problems controlling altitude. Seconds later the tail section, weakened by fire, separated causing uncontrolled descent and in-flight breakup. Fire started from hot-air tube leak at 300°C that damaged electrical insulation causing short circuits.
probable_cause: In-flight fire in cargo bay caused by hot-air tube leak, leading to electrical short circuits and structural failure of the tail section.

factors.evidence: flight attendants reported smoke in the rear section of the cabin
the tail section, weakened by the fire, separated from the aircraft, causing it to enter an uncontrolled descent
air heated to some 300°C escaped, damaging the insulation of electrical wires and the aircraft flight control system
crew reported problems with the elevators

events.text: Interflug flight 450 left Berlin-Schönefeld Airport at 16:30 local time heading southeast towards Czechoslovakia.
At 16:43, thirteen minutes into the flight and 8900 m above the city of Cottbus, the crew reported problems with the elevators.
At 16:51, the crew carried out a fuel dump to decrease landing weight.
Flight attendants reported smoke in the rear section of the cabin.
At 16:59:25, the flight issued a mayday indicating problems controlling the aircraft's altitude.
The tail section, weakened by fire, separated from the aircraft causing it to enter an uncontrolled descent.
Due to the forces of the dive, the rest of the aircraft broke up in mid-air with debris landing in Königs Wusterhausen.

title: Aeroflot 217
summary: Aeroflot Flight 217 was flying at 1200 m when ATC cleared descent to 400 m. The crew confirmed and started to descend normally, but the aircraft failed to level off and passed the 400 m mark at 20 m/s descent rate with engines at low thrust. The aircraft crashed with landing gear up and spoilers retracted. Investigators concluded that the probable cause was psycho-physiological incapacitation of the crew.
probable_cause: Psycho-physiological incapacitation of the crew for reasons unknown, occurring 30-25 seconds before impact.

factors.evidence: pilots either had been incapacitated or lost control of the plane
plane subsequently failed to level off horizontally. It passed the 400 m mark at a vertical velocity of 20 m/s
psycho-physiological incapacitation of the crew for reasons unknown

events.text: The aircraft received instructions from ATC to descend from 1200 m to 400 m.
The crew confirmed and started to descend normally.
The plane subsequently failed to level off horizontally and passed the 400 m mark at a vertical velocity of 20 m/s.
The aircraft crashed shortly afterwards with landing gear up, spoilers retracted and a horizontal speed of about 620 km/h.

title: Eastern Air Lines 401
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crashed in the Florida Everglades shortly before midnight after the autopilot inadvertently disconnected. A subtle bump of the yoke switched the autopilot from altitude hold to Control Wheel Steering mode. While the crew was focused on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, they did not notice the autopilot disconnection and the aircraft gradually lost altitude until striking the ground.
probable_cause: A subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode. The crew's focus on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light distracted them from noticing the altitude loss.

factors.evidence: A subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode, causing the aircraft to begin a descent.
Due to the focus on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, the pilots did not notice the autopilot being shut off.
The aircraft gradually lost altitude and the altitude warning C-chord chime was triggered but there was no indication the pilots had heard it.
Flight 401 crashed west-northwest of Miami, 18.7 mi from the end of Runway 9L.

events.text: After lowering the gear, Stockstill noticed that the landing gear indicator, a green light, had not illuminated.
Loft instructed Stockstill to put the L-1011 on autopilot and a subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode.
The altitude warning C-chord chime located under Repo's workstation was triggered as the aircraft lost altitude.
Flight 401 crashed west-northwest of Miami, 18.7 mi from the end of Runway 9L.
